original_facts.fact: The original History panel offers Hour through Year plus All, previous/next period offsets, separate overall payload Down/Up totals, two colored Down/Up ValueSources, a configurable legend and MultiPlotGraphic sized from the sum of monitor client widths. Source getValue methods are placeholders; refreshHistory supplies graph data explicitly.

Axis byte labels multiply a scaled int by history_scale_div and format a byte count, not bytes per second. Time labels use SimpleDateFormat with the default locale/time zone (HH:mm, dd HH:mm, MM/dd, or yyyy/MM), not an explicit UTC axis.

A hidden panel returns immediately. Visible resolution is minutes for hour/day, hours for week/month, days for year, or weeks for All. It uses SystemTime.getCurrentTime, rounded period boundaries, configured span/offset and current graph width; it also queries an overall range total.

Each period invokes the LongTermStats Date reader, then selects only ST_DATA_DOWNLOAD (3) and ST_DATA_UPLOAD (1). If a period maps to no pixels its values accumulate into pending totals; values are then repeated across a pixel chunk. Graph arrays therefore depend on visible width and include width aggregation/replication, not fixed 24/7 independent bucket markers.

max_data begins at zero and is raised for positive maxima, then a power-of-two history_scale_div reduces long values before int conversion. This source path is not a full signed-int64 graph contract; no numerical or visual equivalence is claimed for the new signed renderer.

The immutable six-component order is protocol upload, payload upload, protocol download, payload download, DHT upload, DHT download. Current/sliding period constants do not themselves define the new explicit saved UTC selection.

deliberate_native_scope: Only render existing immutable Daily 24 hourly buckets or seven independent UTC daily-file totals. Select payload download index 3 and upload index 1 directly; do not sum counters, compute rates, interpolate, smooth, aggregate weeks, re-read files or invoke a clock/timer.

Unknown snapshot/hour/day totals remain gaps; observed zero is a real marker; signed corrections remain signed. A missing bucket breaks both traces. Known adjacent buckets connect, and isolated values remain visible.

Use fixed UTC labels, byte units, raw exact signed tooltip values, and finite coordinates throughout the signed-int64 input domain. New rendering need not match original width-dependent period queries, scale division, default-zone labels, overall totals or legend preferences.

Existing lazy date/mode/session/request admission and hidden/minimized deferral remain intact. New charts consume already accepted snapshots and do not add workers, leases, network, accounting or persistence.

Keep prior 2550 and 3150 Java scalar comparisons independently frozen, without adding them into a new corpus or granting any new Java runtime, chart, missingness, strict-policy, full-owner or global-history equality credit.
